intro: Aspect Ratio takes a width and height like 1920x1080 and reduces it to its simplest aspect ratio (16:9) using the greatest common divisor, plus the exact decimal ratio. It is handy when you need to figure out the proportional ratio of a resolution, image, or video frame without doing the math by hand. Accepts the x, X, or : separator and works entirely in your browser.
useCases: Convert a screen resolution such as 1920x1080 into its simplified 16:9 aspect ratio
Check whether two image or video sizes share the same proportions by comparing their ratios
Get the exact decimal ratio (width / height) for CSS or layout calculations
Verify a thumbnail or crop dimension matches a target aspect ratio before exporting
Quickly simplify odd resolutions like 1366x768 to compare them against standard formats

faq.q: Is my data sent to a server?
faq.a: No. The tool runs entirely in your browser and nothing is uploaded. The width and height you enter never leave your device.

faq.q: What input format does it accept?
faq.a: Enter exactly two numbers separated by x, X, or a colon, for example 1920x1080, 1920X1080, or 1920:1080. Both values must be positive integers.
It returns two lines: the simplified ratio (for example 16:9) computed from the greatest common divisor, and the decimal ratio of width divided by height rounded to four decimal places.

faq.q: Why do I get an error?
faq.a: You will see an error if the input does not contain exactly two parts split by x, X, or :, or if either value is not a positive whole number. Decimals, zero, and negative numbers are rejected.

faq.q: Does it support decimal or fractional dimensions?
faq.a: No. Both width and height must be positive integers, so values like 1920.5 will produce an error.
